classificationReport.dropPolicy: Classification never drops. All 19 sanitized findings are present, one-to-one, with originalId preserved.
classificationReport.severityChangeNote: No input severity was moved. Every band was re-derived from the C4 definitions rather than inherited; the four judgement calls the brief singled out are adjudicated in full below and in each finding.

judgementCalls.question: Do the required preconditions defeat the C4 "no hypotheticals" bar for High?
judgementCalls.reasoning: The two preconditions are ordinary, not extraordinary. (a) The stablecoin approval to Antimatter is MANDATORY to annihilate at all - annihilateFrom pulls the stablecoin from `from` at :222 - so it is universal among users rather than an attacker-awaited coincidence; the max-approval pattern that makes the loss total is the normal way to use such a contract. (b) An antimatter allowance is a plain ERC20 approve, and third-party annihilation is a documented, shipped, unit-tested flow (test/Annihilation.t.sol:130-141). Neither is a "hand-wavy hypothetical"; both are the protocol operating as designed. What is NOT designed is that one allowance authorises a second asset movement plus unrestricted redirection of the ~2x proceeds. Result: direct uncompensated theft of a named victim by a named attacker in one transaction, no privilege, no market condition, no timing. That is the C4 High definition met literally. Source re-verified at lib/antimatter/src/Antimatter.sol:214-237: the sole _spendAllowance is over antimatter. Evidence is unusually strong for a High (PoC + 2 invariant engines + clean Medusa shrink + deterministic replay + Halmos refutation over the whole amount domain), so no part of the claim rests on assertion.

judgementCalls.question: Does the unbounded unbacked mint stay Medium for the current code?
judgementCalls.verdict: MEDIUM - HELD, with an explicit re-weigh trigger
judgementCalls.reasoning: Weighed both directions. Against High: no atomic attack and no specific victim - annihilation is one-way, the actor must hold antimatter and part with real stablecoin, and the harm is diffuse peg dilution realised only through a market sale; decisively, in the CURRENT tree emission is owner-gated (approved minters only), so there is no permissionless drain today and antimatter is not even wired into staging - this is a POLICY exposure, and calling it High would be overstatement, a pipeline-reject condition. Against Low: the liability is real, permanent, unbounded and entirely unaccounted, it lands on non-consenting phUSD holders, and phUSD has no redemption path anywhere (verified) - which means it never trips an insolvency check that would force attention; there is no on-chain control over the exposure and not even an on-chain measurement of it. C4 Medium ("value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements") is the exact fit. Intended-by-design is not a mitigant: Law 1 overrides Law 2, specStatus is FAITHFUL-BUT-UNSAFE, and the NatSpec that states the intent is itself economically false (F-03).
judgementCalls.reweighTrigger: HIGH if a permissionless or automated/high-volume minter is ever approved via setApprovedMinter (:151) - the owner gate is the only thing holding this at Medium. Also re-weigh on any bug in an approved minter (no supply ceiling at :179 converts it directly to unbacked phUSD), or if a phUSD redemption path is ever built (converts peg pressure into on-chain insolvency).

judgementCalls.question: Is the arming misconfiguration "obvious" (invalid under Law 3) or "surprising" (valid footgun), and does permissionless post-arming exploitation change the band?
judgementCalls.reasoning: SURPRISING, not obvious, and the asymmetry proves it: the identical mistake in the other direction (decimals overstated) fails CLOSED with a revert on balance, so an owner has positive reason to believe the parameter is self-checking. The dangerous direction is instead absorbed in silence - both contracts make the same error so it cancels inside calculateMintAmount, the :230 residue check and :233 receipt both pass, and there is no revert, no event anomaly, no on-chain signal at all. A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised => footgun => in scope. This overrides the faithfulness tier's Law-3 suppression of the same item as an "obvious single-step act". Post-arming the exploit IS permissionless, deterministic and unbounded - genuinely High-shaped - and that is why it is at the TOP of the Medium band rather than the bottom. It stays Medium only because the path is not free of external requirements: it needs a misconfiguration that no observed deployment has, which is textbook Medium ("hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements"). Escalate to High on evidence of any live registration whose decimals disagrees with IERC20Metadata.

noOverstatementCheck.basis: Exactly one High, and it is the only finding with a demonstrated one-transaction theft of a named victim by a named attacker with no external requirements. Every other candidate (M-01 permissionless free mint, M-02 unbounded unbacked liability) was tested against High and held at Medium because each needs an external requirement - a misconfiguration, or an owner-approved emission source - that no observed deployment satisfies. findings.label: H-01
findings.title: An ERC20 allowance over ANTIMATTER is silently a dual-asset authority: it lets a third party spend the grantor's STABLECOIN and keep the entire ~2x phUSD proceeds

classification.assetImpact: The grantor's ENTIRE stablecoin balance approved to Antimatter (in practice the full balance, since a max-approval is the only way to use the contract more than once) is pulled out uncompensated, plus the antimatter itself. Both the ~1x antimatter-leg phUSD and the ~1x stable-leg phUSD - the whole ~2x proceeds - are delivered to an attacker-chosen address. Victim receives nothing.
attackPath: 1. Victim approves Antimatter to spend her stablecoin. This is MANDATORY - annihilateFrom pulls the stablecoin via safeTransferFrom(from, address(this), stableAmount) at :222, so no holder can ever annihilate without it. Universal among users, not a special condition.

2. Victim grants an ordinary ERC20 antimatter allowance to a third party - a keeper, router, or any counterparty. The project ships this as a supported flow (test/Annihilation.t.sol:130-141 test_thirdPartySpendsAntimatterAllowance) and NatSpec :189-192 advertises acting on someone else's behalf.
3. Attacker calls annihilateFrom(stable, victim, attacker, amount). :214 spends ONLY the antimatter allowance; :215 burns the victim's antimatter.

4. :222 debits a SECOND asset - the victim's stablecoin - on Antimatter's own standing approval from `from`. No stablecoin allowance from victim to attacker is checked or spent (confirmed at source: the only _spendAllowance call is over antimatter).
5. :236 mints `amount` phUSD to `recipient` and :237 transfers `mintedForStable` to `recipient`; `recipient` is validated only against address(0), so the attacker names himself.
6. One transaction, no flash loan, no admin, no market condition, repeatable up to the allowance.
classification.likelihood: High. Executable by any allowance grantee at will; deterministic; no timing, price, or privilege dependency. The only 'trigger' is the victim doing two things the protocol requires and documents.
classification.assumptions: Victim holds antimatter and a registered stablecoin; both are prerequisites of using the contract at all.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond the two ordinary approvals in steps 1-2. No owner action, no third contract, no adversarial market.

findings.justification: HELD AT HIGH after explicitly testing the 'no hypotheticals' bar as instructed. Neither precondition is extraordinary: (a) the stablecoin approval to Antimatter is not a user choice an attacker must wait for, it is a hard requirement of ever annihilating, so every real user has it; (b) an antimatter allowance is a plain ERC20 approve, and the project's own test suite asserts third-party annihilation is intended behaviour. The defect is precisely that one grant of authority silently carries a second - approve(bob, N) on antimatter is de facto also approve(bob, toStableAmount(N)) on every stablecoin the grantor approved to Antimatter, plus an unrestricted right to redirect the ~2x proceeds. That is direct, uncompensated theft of a specific victim's assets by a specific attacker along a fully concrete path, which is the C4 High definition. Downgrade arguments considered and rejected: 'user error / phishing' does not apply because the victim's action is exactly what the documentation and tests tell her to do and the harm is invisible at approval time; 'approve race / safeApprove front-running' does not apply because nothing is racing - the authority is over-broad by construction; 'intended design' does not apply because an ERC20 approver cannot consent to a second asset she was never asked about, and Law 1 makes intended-but-exploitable reportable. Evidence quality supports High without hand-waving: passing PoC with exact figures (Alice USDC 100e6 -> 0, phUSD to Bob 200e18, usdc.allowance(alice,bob)==0 throughout), two invariants broken on two independent engines (Foundry 512x150 and Medusa 210,604 calls), a clean 2-call Medusa shrink, a deterministic non-fuzz replay, and a Halmos REFUTATION establishing the defect over the whole amount domain rather than one witness. Source re-read at lib/antimatter/src/Antimatter.sol:214-237 confirms the single _spendAllowance is over antimatter only.
findings.recommendation: Require `recipient == from` whenever `msg.sender != from`. This closes the theft window while preserving both legitimate flows (keeper/router annihilating on your behalf and delivering to you; self-annihilation to another recipient). Alternatives: additionally require and spend `IERC20(stable).allowance(from, msg.sender) >= stableAmount`, or drop the `from` parameter and make annihilation self-only.

notes.mitigationCost: Zero functionality lost: requiring recipient == from when msg.sender != from preserves both legitimate flows (keeper annihilating on your behalf and delivering to you; self-annihilation to a chosen recipient).

test_H01_baselineTransferFromTakesOnlyAM - control: plain transferFrom leaves Alice's USDC at 100e6

findings.label: M-01
findings.title: The pairing ratio is taken on trust from the minter's registered `decimals`; the dangerous direction fails OPEN and is permissionlessly exploitable

classification.assetImpact: While armed, any antimatter holder mints ~2x phUSD while surrendering ~1e-10 of the stablecoin. The stable leg - the half that is supposed to be fully collateralised - becomes backed by dust. Unbounded in size (up to all outstanding antimatter) and unbounded in time (no revert, no event anomaly, no on-chain signal). Loss lands on phUSD holders as collateral dilution.
attackPath: 0. ARMING (owner, unknowing): an 18-decimal stablecoin is registered in PhusdStableMinter with decimals understated (e.g. 6). One mistyped argument.
1. Antimatter reads that value verbatim at :250 and never cross-checks IERC20Metadata(stable).decimals(), although it holds the token address and one staticcall would settle it.
2. scale becomes 1e12, so toStableAmount collapses the stablecoin pull by 1e12x. BOTH contracts make the identical error, so it cancels inside calculateMintAmount and nothing reverts.
3. Any holder calls annihilateFrom: 100 AM + 1e8 raw units of an 18-dp stablecoin -> 200e18 phUSD. The :230 residue check and the :233 non-zero receipt both pass.
4. Repeat permissionlessly until the misconfiguration is noticed by some out-of-band means.
classification.likelihood: Low to arm (a deliberate single owner argument that is normally correct), then HIGH and permissionless once armed, with no self-limiting mechanism and no signal that would prompt anyone to look.
classification.assumptions: A registered stablecoin's `decimals` is understated relative to its true ERC20 decimals. Antimatter emission is live enough that some holder has antimatter.
classification.externalRequirements: The owner misconfiguration at registration time (in PhusdStableMinter.registerStablecoin, a nested-submodule contract; filed against Antimatter because Antimatter acts on the value, doubles the blast radius with a second uncollateralised leg, and can defend itself in one line).

findings.justification: FOOTGUN TEST (Law 3) - VALID, NOT SUPPRESSED. The misconfiguration is SURPRISING, not obvious, and the asymmetry is what proves it: the SAME mistake in the other direction (decimals overstated) fails CLOSED - the pull is 1e12x too large and safeTransferFrom reverts on balance. An owner who has seen, or reasonably expects, a loud revert from a wrong decimals argument has every reason to believe the parameter is self-checking. Instead the dangerous direction is silently absorbed at full phUSD issuance. A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised; surprise => footgun => in scope. This explicitly OVERRIDES the faithfulness tier's Law-3 suppression of the same item as 'the minter owner's obvious single-step act' - it is not obvious, because it is silent. SEVERITY - MEDIUM, and the reason it is not High is stated plainly rather than hedged: the post-arming exploit IS permissionless, deterministic and unbounded, which is High-shaped, but the path is not free of external requirements - it needs a misconfiguration that does not exist in any observed deployment. C4 Medium is exactly 'value leak with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements'. It is not Low because the consequence is neither dust nor cosmetic: it is an unbounded permissionless free mint against the collateral base, PoC'd, with an intentional control (the exactness guard, machine-proven sound by Halmos) that provides no protection at all here because the guard is correct GIVEN a correct decimals - the proof is precisely why the registered value carries the whole risk. It is also not a 'weird ERC20' finding: the token is standard; the defect is unvalidated trust in a registered value.
findings.recommendation: In toStableAmount cross-check the registered value: `if (decimals != IERC20Metadata(stable).decimals()) revert DecimalsMismatch(...)` (try/catch, revert if the token has no decimals()). This makes the dangerous direction fail closed like the safe one already does.
findings.reweighTrigger: Escalate to HIGH on evidence that any live or staged registration has a decimals value differing from IERC20Metadata(stable).decimals(). At that point the external requirement is satisfied and the remaining path is permissionless.

tests: test_M_decimalsUnderstatedIsSilentlyExploitable - 18-dp DOLA registered as 6-dp: 100 AM + 1e8 raw DOLA -> 200e18 phUSD, no revert

evidence.symbolicContext: halmos PROVED toStableAmount's exactness guard is sound for d=6 and for symbolic d<=18 (tier3/halmos-p1-d6.txt, halmos-p1-symbolicd.txt) - i.e. the arithmetic is correct GIVEN a correct `decimals`. The proof is exactly why the registered value is the whole risk.

findings.label: M-02
findings.title: Half of every annihilation's phUSD is minted against no incoming value, and the resulting liability is unbounded, unscheduled and unrecorded

classification.assetImpact: Every annihilation mints `amount` phUSD (:236) against no incoming value. The resulting liability is unbounded (mint at :179 has no cap, schedule, or tie to yield or collateral), unscheduled, and recorded nowhere - no contract tracks unbacked phUSD supply. Each outstanding antimatter token is a permanent exercisable ~$1 call on the phUSD collateral pool. The loss is realised as peg dilution borne by phUSD holders and by whatever protocol-owned liquidity absorbs the annihilator's sell.
attackPath: 1. Receive N antimatter free as a staking reward (:180, approved-minter gated).
2. Acquire N (rescaled) stablecoin at ~$1 - REAL capital the actor must part with.
3. annihilateFrom(stable, self, self, N): burn N AM, surrender $N of stable, receive ~2N phUSD.
4. Sell 2N phUSD into protocol-owned liquidity at price p. Net = 2Np - N, profitable for all p > 0.50 (generally p > 1/(1 + exchangeRate/1e18)).
5. Recycle. 100% return per cycle at p = $1.00, permissionless, no flash loan - and it keeps paying arbitrageurs until phUSD reaches half peg.
classification.likelihood: Certain to be exercised once antimatter is emitted at volume - it is not an attack, it is the token's designed use, and it is rational for every holder. Currently gated by how much antimatter exists, which is an undecided policy variable.
classification.assumptions: phUSD trades meaningfully above $0.50; there is liquidity to sell 2N phUSD into; antimatter is emitted in quantity.
classification.externalRequirements: An approved minter must actually emit antimatter (setApprovedMinter, :151). PARK-003 records that antimatter is NOT yet wired into phoenix-phase-2-staging, so emission policy is entirely undecided on-chain.

findings.justification: MEDIUM for the CURRENT code, as filed - weighed against both an upgrade and a downgrade. Not HIGH: there is no atomic attack and no specific victim. Annihilation is one-way and the actor must actually hold antimatter and actually part with real stablecoin, so nothing is stolen in a transaction; the harm is diffuse dilution realised only through market sale. Crucially for the CURRENT tree, emission is owner-gated - only approved minters mint antimatter - so no permissionless drain exists today. Labelling this High now would be overstatement of a policy exposure, and overstatement is a pipeline-reject condition. Not LOW/QA: the liability is real, permanent, unbounded and completely unaccounted; it lands on parties who never consented; phUSD has NO redemption path anywhere (verified), which means this never surfaces as on-chain insolvency that some mechanism would catch - it surfaces only as peg pressure, with no on-chain control and not even an on-chain OBSERVATION of the exposure. An unmeasured unbounded liability is not a state-handling nit. C4 Medium - 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements' - fits exactly. INTENDED DESIGN IS NOT A DEFENCE (Law 1 over Law 2): specStatus is FAITHFUL-BUT-UNSAFE. The declared intent at :188-189 and in CLAUDE.md is implemented precisely; the intent itself is the hazard, so it is filed as a spec-level security finding and dual-channelled to spec-conformance as F-04. In-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority. Law-2 intent is UNGRADED, not passed: no storyDir and no [story-NNN] on any of the 6 commits (PARK-002). The standing Phoenix rule 'externally-derived yield over-payment is opportunity cost, not loss' was checked and does NOT apply - this is dilution of the phUSD collateral base, not over-payment of a reward budget.
recommendation: Treat Antimatter.totalSupply() as the protocol's unbacked-phUSD liability and expose it as such - at minimum a view reporting it next to phUSD.totalSupply().
Bound emission at the source: a supply cap or per-period mint budget on :179, so the liability cannot be enlarged by a single call from any approved minter.
If the intended policy is that emission is budgeted against realised protocol yield, enforce it on-chain - the code has no representation of that policy at all.
Correct the NatSpec at :18 (tracked separately as DEDUP-015).
findings.reweighTrigger: RE-WEIGH AS HIGH if antimatter emission is ever wired to a PERMISSIONLESS or automated/high-volume minter via setApprovedMinter (:151). At that point step 1 of the loop stops being owner-gated and the finding becomes an active, self-serve drain on the phUSD collateral base rather than a policy exposure. Secondary trigger, carried from MR-04: a bug in ANY approved minter contract converts directly into unbacked phUSD, because there is no supply ceiling at :179. Tertiary trigger: if a phUSD redemption path is ever built, the exposure converts from peg pressure into on-chain insolvency and must be re-weighed immediately.

evidence.invariantQuantification: invariant_04 PASSES as an EXACT equality over 76,800 calls in both decimal regimes: phUSD.totalSupply() minus stablecoin in custody (18dp-normalised) == cumulative antimatter burned. The pass is not an all-clear - it is the measurement that the uncollateralised leg is exactly 1:1 with antimatter burned, no rounding drift. invariant_05 separately confirms every stablecoin unit pulled reached strategy custody.
evidence.scopeLimit: invariants 04/05 pin exchangeRate at 1e18; rate divergence is DEDUP-005's territory.

findings.label: M-03
findings.title: PhusdStableMinter's daily phUSD issuance cap governs only half the phUSD an annihilation issues: a cap of X permits 2X

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. The impact is on the protocol's ONLY per-day issuance control: a maxMintPerDay of X permits 2X of phUSD to be issued, and the mis-sizing is invisible because the counter reports 100% utilisation at 50% of real issuance. Antimatter has no cap of its own, no pause, and mint() (:179) has no supply ceiling, so this rail is the sole quantitative bound on the uncollateralised issuance of DEDUP-004/M-02.
attackPath: 1. Operator sets maxMintPerDay = X for a stablecoin, intending X phUSD/day of issuance.
2. Antimatter routes only the stable leg through PhusdStableMinter.mint (:227), which charges the counter amount*rate/1e18.
3. The antimatter leg is minted by Antimatter itself at :236 on its own FlaxToken authorisation, where the counter cannot see it. Issuance is amount*(1 + rate/1e18).
4. In ONE transaction the intended cap is exceeded outright - deterministic replay: cap 10,000e18, a single annihilateFrom of 6,000e18 charges 6,000e18 but delivers 12,000e18.
classification.likelihood: Certain - it is not conditional on anything; every annihilation under-charges by exactly the same factor.
classification.assumptions: exchangeRate == 1e18 gives the flat 2x; the true divisor is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18) and moves with the rate (see M-04).
classification.externalRequirements: maxMintPerDay set non-zero, i.e. the operator is relying on the rail at all.

findings.justification: ADJUDICATING THE CONFLICT the sanitizer flagged (CODE-003 conceded 'a downgrade to Low is defensible'). HELD AT MEDIUM. The Low argument is honest - no asset loss and no attacker-specific gain - but it mis-frames the impact class: C4 Medium covers 'the function of the protocol ... could be impacted', and the function impaired here IS a safety control. The protocol's only issuance rail is off by 2x in the unsafe direction, silently, on a token half of whose issuance is structurally uncollateralised; and the operator has no way to notice, because the counter reads fully utilised exactly when it has permitted double. A control that lies about its own utilisation is worse than an absent control, because it manufactures false confidence at the moment it matters most. FOOTGUN TEST (Law 3): a competent, non-malicious operator entering X as a daily phUSD issuance cap WOULD be surprised that 2X is issued; discovering it requires knowing a second contract holds an independent FlaxToken mint authorisation. Surprise => footgun => in scope, at honest severity. Not High: no theft, no specific victim, no attacker gain beyond what the design already grants. Evidence: two invariants broken on two independent engines, a Medusa counterexample measuring exactly 2.000x in a single call, a deterministic non-fuzz replay, and an anti-vacuity check confirming the minter's cap was LIVE in the harness (121 swallowed inner reverts dominated by 'Daily mint limit exceeded') - so the failure is not an artefact of an inert control. Deliberately NOT collapsed with M-01/DEDUP-003 (unvalidated decimals) or M-05/DEDUP-006 (shared-budget DoS): same neighbourhood, different root causes and different mitigations.
findings.recommendation: Route the antimatter leg through PhusdStableMinter so one counter sees the whole issuance, or add an equivalent per-period cap on Antimatter's own leg at :236, or (weakest) rename/document maxMintPerDay as a per-stable DEPOSIT throttle so operators size it correctly.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: PRESERVED FROM ECON-002 VERBATIM: 'Until the code is changed, set maxMintPerDay to HALF the phUSD issuance you intend to permit, for every stablecoin that Antimatter can annihilate - and only while exchangeRate == 1e18. The correct divisor is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18), so it changes the moment the rate is moved (see DEDUP-005). Do not treat maxMintPerDay as a phUSD-issuance cap; it is a per-stable deposit throttle that happens to be denominated in phUSD.'

findings.label: M-04
findings.title: exchangeRate re-prices only the stable leg: a hard 1x issuance floor no setting can go below, an unbounded ceiling, and a silent re-scaling of what maxMintPerDay permits

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. Two operational impacts: (a) the natural remediation lever for over-issuance does not work - at exchangeRate = 0.10e18 the protocol still emits 1.10 phUSD per $1 taken in, and the uncollateralised component is entirely unaffected, so there is NO rate that makes annihilation backing-neutral and the only true stop is setStablecoinEnabled(false), a full stop with no intermediate setting; (b) changing the rate silently re-scales what maxMintPerDay permits (at rate 0.5e18 the effective multiplier moves from 2x to 3x the entered number), so the M-03 mis-sizing drifts underneath the operator.
attackPath: 1. Operator observes phUSD dilution and reaches for exchangeRate as a throttle - the obvious lever.

2. The stablecoin PULLED is rate-independent (decimals only, :254-256) and the antimatter leg is always exactly `amount` (:236); only the stable leg's phUSD is rate-scaled. Total issuance per unit of stablecoin received is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18), which is bounded BELOW by 1x.
3. Dilution continues at >= 1x forever while the operator believes the throttle is engaged.
4. Simultaneously the daily cap's effective multiplier has changed without any change to maxMintPerDay, and neither side documents the coupling.
classification.likelihood: Medium - it bites exactly when an operator responds to an issuance problem, i.e. at the worst moment.
classification.assumptions: Operator treats exchangeRate as an issuance throttle, which is what its name and position suggest.
classification.externalRequirements: An owner rate change. Non-malicious and non-obvious in its consequences.

findings.justification: MEDIUM as an operational hazard, with the boundary stated explicitly so this is not read as an owner-malice finding. The 'unbounded ceiling' half alone (rate = 1.5e18 emits 2.5 phUSD per $1 from one un-timelocked owner call) would be LOW on its own - an owner raising a rate and getting more issuance is an OBVIOUS consequence, and Law 3 suppresses obvious owner misuse. The Medium rests entirely on the two SURPRISING halves: that lowering the rate can never reach parity (a safety lever that silently cannot do the job it appears to do), and that a rate change silently re-prices a different control. Neither is documented on either side. Surprise => footgun => in scope at honest severity, and 'the protocol's issuance control does not function as a control' is a C4 Medium function impact. Not High: no theft, no direct asset risk, requires an owner action, and the harm is realised only through the dilution channel already priced in M-02. The Halmos PROOF that the no-residue property holds for EVERY uint256 exchangeRate is retained as scoping evidence, not as reassurance: it establishes that an arbitrary rate does not strand assets, which isolates the hazard as economic/operational rather than a settlement defect.
recommendation: Add a sanity bound in Antimatter itself - it already reads exchangeRate's sibling fields at :250 and can assert mintedForStable is within tolerance of `amount`, so a fat-fingered or oversized rate fails closed.
Alternatively scale the antimatter leg by the same rate at :236 so the single knob governs the whole output.
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Treat exchangeRate as an amplitude control on the BACKED leg only, never as an issuance throttle. Keep it at or below 1e18 on every annihilatable stablecoin. Recompute maxMintPerDay as intendedIssuance / (1 + exchangeRate/1e18) on every rate change. To actually stop dilution use setStablecoinEnabled(false).

evidence.symbolic: halmos PROVED (tier3/halmos-p2-noresidue-unbounded.txt) the no-residue property holds for EVERY uint256 exchangeRate - i.e. an arbitrary rate does not strand assets. The hazard is economic, not a settlement defect, which this proof isolates.
evidence.profitabilityBoundary: the annihilator's loop (DEDUP-004) stays profitable whenever p > 1/(1 + rate/1e18): p > $1.00 at rate 0, p > $0.50 at rate 1e18.

findings.label: M-05
findings.title: Annihilation and ordinary phUSD minting share one daily budget, and the annihilation path extracts 2x per unit of budget - griefing the on-ramp is the most profitable use of it

classification.assetImpact: Availability, not assets. The protocol's ordinary permissionless stablecoin->phUSD on-ramp is deniable for a given stablecoin for the remainder of a 24h window, by an actor who is PAID for doing it: an ordinary minter gets 1 phUSD per unit of shared budget, an annihilator gets 2. The DoS costs nothing because it is a side effect of a profitable trade. Window-reset semantics (restart on the first mint after expiry, not a fixed schedule) additionally hand the annihilator control over when each window opens.
attackPath: 1. Annihilator holds antimatter and the registered stablecoin.
2. Calls annihilateFrom sized to consume the remaining config.mintedToday budget at :227 - the identical counter the general on-ramp charges.
3. Ordinary depositors are refused ('Daily mint limit exceeded') for the rest of the window while the annihilator has extracted 2x per unit of budget consumed.
4. By timing the first mint after expiry, the annihilator also chooses when the next window starts.
classification.likelihood: Medium-high once antimatter is emitted - the griefing is not an extra cost, it is the most profitable way to use the budget, so a rational annihilator does it by default.
classification.assumptions: maxMintPerDay is set non-zero for the stablecoin; the annihilator holds enough antimatter to consume the window's budget.
classification.externalRequirements: Live antimatter emission (same PARK-003 caveat as M-02) and a non-zero cap.

findings.justification: C4 Medium on the availability limb: 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted'. The external requirements are real and stated (emission must be live, cap non-zero), which is exactly what Medium permits and what keeps it off High - there is no theft, the condition self-resolves each window, and no user loses funds. Not Low, because denying the protocol's general on-ramp at zero marginal cost to a party the protocol is simultaneously paying is a structural incentive defect, not an incidental one. Confidence is medium and is recorded as such. Deliberately NOT collapsed with M-03: same counter, different root cause (under-counting vs profitable budget exhaustion), different impact class, different mitigation - collapsing would bury the DoS.
recommendation: Give the annihilation path its own budget, or charge the antimatter leg too (which also fixes DEDUP-002) so the two paths consume budget proportionally to what they issue.
Use a fixed epoch boundary to remove the first-minter timing control.

findings.label: M-06
findings.title: Post-conditions confirm the stablecoin LEFT, never that the yield strategy CREDITED it; on a current-master strategy the stable leg is minted against principal that was not fully credited

classification.assetImpact: IF the claim holds against the deployed code: the stable leg's phUSD is sized from `amount`, never from what the yield strategy actually credited, so phUSD would be issued against principal that was not fully credited - an unquantified backing shortfall. Size UNKNOWN and unmeasured.
attackPath: (NOT DEMONSTRATED - diff-only reasoning; the DEPLOYED yield-strategy/vault version is unknown because the nested vault pin 043ff2c is 11 commits behind vault master 0110ce4.)
1. PhusdStableMinter makes a bare statement call to IYieldStrategy.deposit and discards its return value.
2. Antimatter's post-conditions cannot catch a shortfall: :230 asserts only that the stablecoin LEFT Antimatter, and :232-233 measure a phUSD delta and require it merely to be NON-ZERO.
3. On a current-master strategy that credits less than the deposited principal, the difference is unbacked. Whether any DEPLOYED strategy behaves this way is UNVERIFIED.
classification.likelihood: UNKNOWN. Not established against any deployed contract.
classification.assumptions: That the DEPLOYED yield strategy is a vault-master-tree build (0110ce4-era, deposit() returning creditedPrincipal) rather than a 043ff2c-era build. If the deployed strategy is the 043ff2c-era build there is NO finding at all. This is a question about the deployed STRATEGY/VAULT version, not about the minter, whose pin is current.
classification.externalRequirements: A yield strategy whose deposit credits less than the principal transferred.

findings.justification: CLASSIFIED BUT PARKED, per instruction, and the label must not be read as a verdict. The Medium label is carried forward from the highest input severity (ECON-004 medium over CODE-006 low, per the conflicting-severity rule) as a PLACEHOLDER for triage ordering only. This finding is diff-only: the minter pin is CURRENT (d6ed1156 == its remote master tip), but the nested vault pin (043ff2c) is 11 commits behind vault master (0110ce4), so the DEPLOYED yield-strategy/vault version is unknown - and the standing 'nested submodule pin stale trap' rule says cross-repo claims must be read from the deployed/top-level sibling checkout, because nested lib/mutable/** is stale by construction. It is therefore not adjudicable in this run and MUST NOT be submitted, PoC'd as fact, or cited as a known shortfall until the manual-review action is completed. It is kept in a visible channel rather than dropped (Law 1: recall beats report-tidiness). NOTE the recommendation that survives independently of the parked claim and can be actioned now: replace the unbounded `mintedForStable == 0` check at :233 with a two-sided assertion against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount). That same mitigation is shared with L-01 and F-01, which are NOT parked.
findings.recommendation: Independently of the above: replace the unbounded `mintedForStable == 0` check at :233 with a two-sided assertion against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount), so a short or unexpected mint reverts rather than silently shortchanging the annihilator.
findings.verificationStatus: UNVERIFIED - severity label is PROVISIONAL and carries NO verification weight
findings.manualReviewAction: RE-CHECK INSTRUCTION: read the DEPLOYED yield strategy (resolved from chain, for the stablecoins actually registered) and measure creditedPrincipal vs amount there. DO NOT re-check the phUSD-stable-minter pin - it is already current and would wrongly read as the park being resolved. If the deployed strategy is 043ff2c-era behaviour (no return / full credit), close as not-applicable; if it credits less than the principal transferred, size the stable leg from the returned value and/or assert mintedForStable against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount).
findings.parkRationaleCorrection: PARK RATIONALE CORRECTED 2026-08-18 (review pass): it is NOT true that the phUSD-stable-minter pin is stale - antimatter pins lib/phUSD-stable-minter at d6ed1156, which IS that repo's remote master tip, so THE MINTER PIN IS CURRENT. The stale layer is one level deeper: lib/phUSD-stable-minter/lib/vault is pinned at 043ff2c while vault's remote master is 0110ce4 (11 commits ahead, incl. stories 043/044/048/049, which introduced deposit() returning creditedPrincipal). What cannot be adjudicated at this commit is therefore WHICH YIELD-STRATEGY / VAULT VERSION IS ACTUALLY DEPLOYED, because the finding depends on the deployed strategy's deposit() return behaviour, not on the minter's version.

findings.label: L-01
findings.title: mintedForStable is a balance delta, not an attribution: any phUSD arriving mid-call is forwarded to the caller-chosen recipient

classification.assetImpact: phUSD arriving at Antimatter mid-call is swept to the caller-chosen recipient as free value. PoC: 500 phUSD injected from a stablecoin's transfer hook, annihilator walks away with 700e18 instead of 200e18.
attackPath: 1. Owner registers a stablecoin whose transfer hook can push phUSD to Antimatter.
2. Annihilator calls annihilateFrom; the hook fires inside the :220-:232 measurement window.
3. mintedForStable is a balance DELTA, never compared to minter.calculateMintAmount, and is forwarded wholesale at :237.
classification.likelihood: Low - requires a registered hook-bearing stablecoin, which no observed registration has.
classification.assumptions: A hook-bearing token is registered as a supported stablecoin.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner registration of such a token.

findings.justification: Low. The mechanism is real and PoC'd, but every path to it runs through a token property no registered stablecoin has, and the value swept is value that had to arrive from somewhere in the first place. Not suppressed as 'weird ERC20' - the point is the asymmetry in Antimatter's own discipline: on the stablecoin side the measured-balance pattern is what makes :230 fail CLOSED, while on the phUSD side the identical pattern converts an unexpected inbound into a payout instead of a revert. Related to MR-01 (parked) and shares its mitigation with M-06/F-01.
findings.recommendation: Compute the expected stable leg from minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount) and use the balance delta only as an equality assertion, so an unexpected inbound reverts rather than paying out.

tests: test_midCallPhUSDInjectionIsForwardedToRecipient - 500e18 injected from the stable's hook; annihilator receives 700e18
test_preExistingPhUSDDonationIsNotSwept - control: a pre-call 500e18 donation is correctly excluded by the :220 snapshot and remains stuck (rescueERC20-able)

findings.label: L-02
findings.title: Once phUSD and the minter are both wired, the phUSD address can never be changed - the two setters mutually lock

classification.assetImpact: No funds at risk. A phUSD redeployment would force a full Antimatter redeployment, losing all antimatter balances (non-upgradeable, no migration path).
attackPath: 1. Owner wires phUSD and the minter.

2. setPhUSD refuses any address the configured minter does not mint; setPhUSDMinter refuses any minter that does not mint the configured phUSD; PhusdStableMinter.phUSD is immutable; neither setter accepts address(0) to unwire.
3. No ordering of calls reaches a different phUSD. The pair is permanently welded.
classification.likelihood: Low frequency, but certain if a phUSD migration is ever needed.
classification.assumptions: phUSD is intended to be permanent, which is why this is Low rather than Medium.

findings.justification: Low, Law-3 footgun. An owner reading two independent setters would reasonably believe either can be re-pointed; discovering the weld only at the moment a migration is needed is a surprise with an expensive remedy - so it is in scope rather than suppressed as centralization. Not Medium: no funds at risk, and the permanence is consistent with intent.
findings.recommendation: Document the one-way property on setPhUSD, or add an owner-only `rewire(IFlax newPhUSD, PhusdStableMinter newMinter)` that sets both atomically and re-checks consistency - preserving the no-drift invariant without welding the pair.

findings.label: L-03
findings.title: A near-zero exchangeRate turns a soft throttle into a hard brick: the stable leg rounds to zero and PhUSDNotReceived kills the whole annihilation

classification.assetImpact: Liveness only, no value loss. exchangeRate = 0 as a soft 'stop paying the stable half' hard-bricks annihilation for that stablecoin; near-zero rates brick it only for small amounts, giving an amount-dependent revert whose error name points at the wrong contract.
attackPath: 1. Owner sets a near-zero exchangeRate.
2. floor(amount * rate / 1e18) truncates to zero, so the stable leg mints nothing.
3. :233's zero-guard reverts the WHOLE annihilation rather than delivering the still-valid antimatter leg.
4. The revert surfaces as PhUSDNotReceived, which reads as 'the minter failed to deliver', not 'your rate setting rounds to zero'.
classification.assumptions: Owner uses a near-zero rate as a soft throttle - a natural reading, and the same misapprehension M-04 documents.
classification.externalRequirements: An owner rate setting near zero.

findings.justification: Low. Liveness only and owner-triggered, but the misdiagnosis cost is the surprising part: the guard is the right instinct (it catches a non-delivering minter) yet doubles as an undiagnosable configuration error pointing at an innocent contract. Footgun, honest severity Low. Adjacent to M-04 but a distinct failure mode (hard brick vs silent non-throttle).
findings.recommendation: Either document PhUSDNotReceived as also covering 'exchangeRate rounds this amount's stable leg to zero', or bound the rate away from zero at registration/update time.

symbolic.note: recorded in symbolic-results.md as reachable only symbolically - 'a fuzzer over sensible rates would not reach it'

findings.label: C-01
findings.title: FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges silently voids every outstanding antimatter claim, and Antimatter exposes no view of its own authorisation status

classification.assetImpact: Every outstanding antimatter token becomes permanently inert on one call from a principal who is not Antimatter's owner and may not be reasoning about antimatter at all. Antimatter is a reward token with no purchase price, so no capital is destroyed - but the entire outstanding claim is.
attackPath: 1. FlaxToken's owner uses the documented global kill switch revokeAllMintPrivileges (mintVersion++).
2. There is no per-minter event and no view on either contract, so nothing signals that Antimatter has been de-authorised.

3. Annihilation is silently dead while ordinary minting still works after re-setMinter on the minter alone; off-chain UIs still see a configured, registered, non-paused system because toStableAmount still returns successfully.
4. Recovery requires re-setMinter on BOTH contracts; forgetting Antimatter leaves the failure latent.
classification.assumptions: FlaxToken owner and Antimatter owner may be different parties, and nothing requires them to coordinate.

findings.justification: Centralization/upstream-privilege finding, filed C-01 at Low. NOT a malicious-owner vector - it is the observability and two-contract-recovery gap around a legitimate emergency lever that makes it a Law-3 footgun: a competent, non-malicious phUSD owner would be surprised that a global kill switch also voids an unrelated token's entire outstanding claim and that recovery needs two contracts. Not Medium: the action is deliberate and emergency-scoped, and antimatter carries no purchase price. Deliberately NOT collapsed with C-02 - same trust structure, different mitigations (an authorisation view + runbook vs an own-owner pause flag).
recommendation: Expose a view on Antimatter reporting whether it is currently an authorised, current-version phUSD minter, so the condition is observable without simulating an annihilation.
Document the two-contract re-authorisation requirement in the incident runbook.

findings.label: C-02
findings.title: Antimatter has no kill switch of its own; every way to halt annihilation belongs to a different principal

classification.assetImpact: No direct impact. Incident-response capability only: if a defect is found in Antimatter itself - including H-01 - its own owner cannot stop it. The fastest available lever (FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges) is global and silently de-authorises PhusdStableMinter too.
attackPath: 1. A live defect in annihilateFrom is discovered.
2. Antimatter is not Pausable and exposes no owner lever to halt annihilation.
3. Halting requires PhusdStableMinter's pauser/owner, FlaxToken's owner, or the yield strategy's owner - all principals independent of Antimatter.owner().
4. The only fast lever is global and causes collateral damage.
classification.likelihood: Conditional on another defect existing - which H-01 demonstrates is not hypothetical.
classification.assumptions: The independent owners are not the same party, which nothing enforces.

findings.justification: Centralization/governance-structure finding, C-02 at QA severity. It causes nothing on its own and is therefore not Medium; it is worth reporting because it is a severity MULTIPLIER on every other finding here - H-01 is a one-transaction theft that Antimatter's own owner has no proportionate lever to stop. Filed as a runbook-or-pause-flag recommendation, not as an owner-trust complaint.
findings.recommendation: Either document the incident-response runbook (who to call, in what order) or add an owner-settable `annihilationPaused` flag checked at the top of annihilateFrom, so the contract's own owner holds a proportionate, non-global lever.

findings.label: F-01
findings.title: The spec's measured-balance discipline is applied in full to the stablecoin leg but only nominally to the phUSD leg: no minimum-output guard on an already-irreversible burn

classification.assetImpact: The holder's antimatter is irreversibly burned at full quantity while the stable half returns almost no phUSD, and the transaction SUCCEEDS. Loss is bounded by the rate divergence, not by anything the caller can specify.
attackPath: 1. Holder submits annihilateFrom.
2. exchangeRate is low, or is changed by the owner between submission and execution.
3. :233 requires only that mintedForStable be NON-ZERO - there is no minOut and no expected-output parameter on an already-irreversible burn.
4. The burn settles at full quantity against a near-empty stable leg.
classification.likelihood: Low - requires a low or concurrently-changed rate. Not adversarially front-runnable for profit; the harm is to the caller.
classification.assumptions: An owner rate change or a low standing rate.
classification.externalRequirements: Rate divergence between submission and execution.

findings.justification: Routed to the SPEC-CONFORMANCE report as F-01, not into the QA bundle (Law 2: a deviation from stated behaviour is never buried in QA/gas noise). The deviation: the contract's own stated discipline is that balances are MEASURED rather than assumed, and that discipline is applied in full to the stablecoin leg (:230 fails closed) but only nominally to the phUSD leg (:233 checks non-zero). Severity Low on the security limb - no attacker gain, caller-borne, bounded - so it is reported at honest Low rather than inflated by its spec status. Shares its mitigation with M-06 and L-01.
findings.recommendation: Add a minOut / expected-phUSD parameter, or assert mintedForStable against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount).

findings.label: F-02
findings.title: The invariant trip-wire CLAUDE.md nominates for 'never expose a burn' is a four-name denylist, not an invariant check

classification.assetImpact: None directly. The project's nominated trip-wire for its own stated invariant ('Antimatter must never expose a burn outside a completed annihilation') is a four-name denylist rather than a property check, so it would not catch a new burn entry point under any name outside that list - including the H-01 path, which violates the invariant from the grantor's ledger while passing the test.
attackPath: 1. CLAUDE.md nominates test_noPublicBurnEntryPoints as the guard for the no-burn invariant.
2. The test probes four hard-coded names (:344-345).
3. Any future burn-exposing function under a different name, or any existing path that is economically a burn, passes silently.
classification.likelihood: N/A - it is a coverage defect, already demonstrated: H-01's invariant violation coexists with a passing test.

findings.justification: Spec-conformance F-02 at Low: the stated invariant is not actually enforced by the artifact the project designates to enforce it. Reported in spec-conformance rather than QA because it is a faithfulness gap in the project's own control, and because a passing test is exactly the kind of false assurance that lets a real defect through - as H-01 shows it already has. No asset impact of its own, hence Low. The Tier-3 harness at workspace/antimatter/test/audit/invariant/ is a ready template for a real property assertion; note that harness is AUDIT-AUTHORED and must never be cited as project coverage or filed as a project file.
findings.recommendation: Replace the name-denylist with a property assertion (totalSupply is non-decreasing across every non-annihilateFrom external call, exercised by fuzzed calldata) or a source assertion (a single _burn occurrence, inside annihilateFrom). The Tier-3 harness at workspace/antimatter/test/audit/invariant/ is a ready template.

findings.label: F-03
findings.title: The contract-header NatSpec justifies the unbacked mint with a redemption symmetry that does not exist, and states a 2x output the code does not guarantee

classification.assetImpact: No direct impact; misleads integrators and reviewers about the collateral position. The contract-header NatSpec (:16-18) justifies the unbacked mint with a redemption symmetry that does not exist and states a flat 2x output the code does not guarantee (the total is exchangeRate-dependent).
attackPath: 1. An integrator or reviewer reads :13-20 and concludes both halves of the payout are redemptions of deposited value.
2. Only the stablecoin half is a redemption; the antimatter half is an uncollateralised mint (M-02).
3. The stated 2x is also not guaranteed - it is (1 + exchangeRate/1e18) (M-04).
classification.likelihood: Certain to mislead any reader who relies on it.

findings.justification: Spec-conformance F-03 at Low. Kept DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from M-02 and NOT folded into it: the root cause is a documentation defect, the remediation is different (correct the NatSpec, not bound the emission), the reader is different (integrators), and - decisively - collapsing it would let the doc defect vanish the moment the economic finding is triaged as accepted-by-design. That separation is the whole point. Consistent with the standing rule that in-source docs carry no suppression authority and, where falsely exhaustive, raise severity rather than lower it: this NatSpec is the ONLY intent artefact this project has (no story, no storyDir), and it is economically inaccurate - which is why M-02's 'it is intended' defence gets no weight.
findings.recommendation: Correct :16-18: only the stablecoin half is a redemption; the antimatter half is an uncollateralised mint. State the exchangeRate dependence of the total rather than a flat 2x.

findings.label: Q-01
findings.title: toStableAmount is a decimals-only rescale and is not a phUSD preview; the local `decimals` also shadows ERC20.decimals()

attackPath: N/A - naming/API clarity.

findings.justification: QA. toStableAmount is a decimals-only input rescale, not a phUSD preview, and its name invites the opposite reading; the local `decimals` also shadows ERC20.decimals(). No exploit path. Worth reporting because the absence of a real preview is what leaves callers with no way to form the expectation F-01 says they cannot assert on.
findings.recommendation: (a) Add previewAnnihilate(address stable, uint256 amount) returns (uint256 stableAmount, uint256 phUSDOut) composing minter.calculateMintAmount, and document toStableAmount as the input-side rescale only. (b) Rename the local to `stableDecimals`.

findings.label: Q-02
findings.title: recipient is guarded against address(0) but not against address(this): an annihilation can come to rest ON the contract

classification.assetImpact: Self-inflicted: the full ~2x payout comes to rest ON Antimatter with the antimatter already burned. Recoverable by the owner via rescueERC20.
attackPath: 1. Caller passes recipient == address(this).
2. :236 mints to Antimatter and :237 transfers from Antimatter to itself.
3. The payout is stranded on the contract.
classification.likelihood: Low - caller error only, no attacker gain.

findings.justification: QA. The C4 'user input mistake' class partially applies and is what holds this at QA rather than higher - correctly, since there is no attacker gain and rescueERC20 recovers it. Not suppressed outright, because the contract already guards address(0) at :203 and its own stated settle-whole-or-not-at-all design implies this case; address(this) is exactly as cheap to reject as address(0).
findings.recommendation: Add `if (recipient == address(this)) revert ...;` alongside the existing zero check - address(this) is exactly as cheap to reject as address(0).

tests: test_recipientSelfStrandsPhUSD - 200e18 phUSD settles on the Antimatter contract, antimatter already burned

findings.label: Q-03
findings.title: approvedMinters() copies the whole EnumerableSet to memory with no bound

attackPath: EnumerableSet.values() is unbounded; an off-chain reader gas-outs once the set grows, and any future on-chain consumer inherits the unbounded loop.

findings.justification: QA. The C4 'unused view functions are QA at best' rule applies as a severity CEILING and the finding was already filed at that ceiling, so the rule changes nothing here. External view only; no on-chain caller is forced through it.
findings.recommendation: Paginate, or keep approvedMinterAt/approvedMinterCount (:169, :164) as the supported iteration path and document values() as off-chain-only.

findings.label: Q-04
findings.title: Static-analysis findings in audit-harness and mock files (test/**)

attackPath: N/A

findings.justification: QA, and self-labelled likely triage-death. Retained rather than suppressed because test/** is first-party and in scope under the default-in-scope denylist, so 'it's only tests' is not a suppression ground - but it carries no security weight and needs no action. Note the 297 static results already filtered upstream are not re-litigated here.
findings.recommendation: None required. If desired, use SafeERC20 in test helpers for consistency.

parkedItems.title: phUSD.totalSupply is transiently inconsistent between the two legs of an annihilation
parkedItems.reason: Between :227 and :236 phUSD.totalSupply reflects one leg of a two-leg issuance while the antimatter is already burned. An external protocol reading phUSD supply as a collateralisation input in that window sees an UNDER-count. Not filed because (a) the quantity belongs to FlaxToken not Antimatter, (b) the only way to execute inside the window is a registered stablecoin's transfer hook at :222, (c) both legs are increases so no observer sees an over-count.
parkedItems.reevaluateIf: a phUSD collateralisation oracle is built, or a hook-bearing stablecoin is registered

parkedItems.title: Registering phUSD itself as a supported stablecoin
parkedItems.reason: Nothing rejects stable == address(phUSD); :219/:220 would snapshot the same balance twice and the :230 residue check and :232 delta would interfere. Not filed: obviously self-defeating configuration (Law 3, obvious misuse => suppress). Recorded so a future reviewer does not re-derive it. A one-line `if (stable == address(_phUSD)) revert` would close it cheaply.

parkedItems.title: Registered-but-not-approveYS'd stablecoin is a liveness trap Antimatter cannot detect
parkedItems.reason: Antimatter's registration test (:251) is yieldStrategy != address(0), which passes as soon as registerStablecoin runs. approveYS is a SEPARATE owner call, and until it is made every annihilation of that stable reverts inside the minter with no signal Antimatter can surface. Liveness only, no value at risk, fix belongs to the minter's registration flow.
parkedItems.action: deployment-runbook item: register and approveYS must be treated as one atomic step

parkedItems.title: Antimatter supply discipline is entirely off-contract
parkedItems.reason: The code-scanner explicitly deferred this to econ-scanner; econ filed it as ECON-001, now DEDUP-004. Kept visible here so the hand-off is auditable and the item is not assumed lost between the two agents.

The substantive defect in these two functions (the mutual lock) IS filed, as DEDUP-009.

parkedItems.title: Three symbolic properties are UNVERIFIED (11 TIMEOUTs) and must not be read as coverage
parkedItems.reason: Recorded at dedup because a TIMEOUT is not a proof and downstream reports must not read silence as coverage (standing rule: symbolic TIMEOUT != proof). (1) End-to-end conservation 'phUSD delivered == amount + stableHalf' TIMED OUT in all 8 configurations, two solvers, bounds from 2**96 down to 2**32 - bound-insensitive, so a narrower domain does not buy a proof. (2) toStableAmount reverts-iff-inexact: the forward exactness direction IS proved; the absence of a spurious revert is not. (3) Overflow parity of the minter's evaluation order is unproven (identical by hand, but that is an argument, not a proof).
parkedItems.additionalScopeLimits: Every full-flow proof pins d=6 (or 18) and rate=1e18 concretely; symbolic decimals and symbolic rate were carried only through the pure-arithmetic properties. Full-flow proofs are bounded at amount < 2**96. External dependencies are audit-authored minimal mocks (the real PhusdStableMinter IS used unmodified). The minter's 24h cap, pause flag and enabled flag are left at permissive defaults. Reentrancy is not a symbolic target.
parkedItems.action: No finding filed - there is nothing to report, only an absence of proof. Parked so no downstream report claims these areas are verified.
